column3: The Hebrew describes the clans as those of “the sons of Joseph” and twice names speaking “before” Moses and the leaders; BSB says “clans of Joseph” and makes Moses and the leaders the people approached and addressed.
The Hebrew repeats “my lord” and changes from active “the LORD commanded” to passive “my lord was commanded”; BSB uses a pronoun for Moses and active divine commanding in both clauses.
The Hebrew describes becoming wives of men from the tribes without an explicit “other”; BSB supplies “the other tribes.”
The Hebrew introduces the Jubilee with “if”; BSB uses “when.”
The Hebrew uses “by the mouth of the LORD”; BSB says “at the word of the LORD.”
The Hebrew repeats the becoming-wives expression and says “the one good in their eyes”; BSB repeats “marry” and says “anyone they please.”
The Hebrew uses the image of clinging to the inheritance; BSB says “retain the inheritance.”
The Hebrew uses the image of clinging to the inheritance; BSB says “retain its inheritance.”
The Hebrew calls their husbands “the sons of their uncles”; BSB says “cousins on their father’s side.”
The Hebrew names “the sons of Manasseh”; BSB says “the descendants of Manasseh.”
The Hebrew says the LORD commanded “by the hand of Moses”; BSB says He “gave” the commands “through Moses.”
